explanation: Mixture with no single theme: Java package/import roots ('org', 'com' after package/import), the word 'game(s)' after 'video', escape characters after a backslash in shell/LaTeX/registry paths (\033, \\, \dfrac, \pm), plus scattered tokens (C++ '<<', getClass, 'Court', 'VAD'). Mid and weak activations look like ordinary prose tokens with no clear pattern.

Mainly fires on words for being formally joined to or granted a status: 'married/marriage (to)', 'elected to', 'issued/granted to' (patents), 'appointed', 'named', 'member', 'logged in (as)', 'confirmed/Confirmation', 'agreeing to'. A smaller unrelated offshoot fires on X.509 certificate tokens ('x509', 'Certificate') and the '-ab' suffix of antibody drug names.

Fires on the first subword fragment of a word that is split into several tokens, mostly a rare surname or given name after a first name (Kar-avelas, Nar-ayan, Kar-loff, Str-ick, C-untz) and the Latin prefix 'extr-' in 'extracellular/extrapulmonary/extrastimulation'. The token has to be an incomplete word stem that gets finished by the next tokens; whole words do not fire.

Fires on function words and operators in the middle of a clause, where the word picks out a contrast, comparison or condition ('same', 'just', 'than', 'without', 'not', 'until', 'after', 'very', 'most'), and on '=' or '*r' in generated algebra problems ('Solve 18 = ...'). It is broad and diffuse, without an obvious single semantic trigger.

Fires strongly on the keyword 'import' (Java/Kotlin/Android) or 'use' (PHP) at the start of a line in a file-header import block, especially after the first import line or after a package/namespace declaration. Weak scattered firing on unrelated tokens such as garbled CJK bytes or 'void'.

Fires at the point where a broad category noun ('various types of information', 'a variety of cells', 'a number of factors', 'several mechanisms') is about to be expanded into examples. Usually that is the comma before 'such as'/'including', but it can also be 'These', 'which', or the category noun itself ('traits', 'forms', 'services'). The context has to set up a list of instances.

Fires on boilerplate structural tokens in source code: the C++ destructor '~' after 'virtual', words inside license header comments ('license information', 'please view', 'can be found', 'or in'), '0' in a for-loop initializer 'i = 0', and other syntax tokens such as 'public:', '__clone' and 'func ('. The common thread is formulaic code and license text where the next token is highly predictable.

Fires on assorted tokens in technical or reference text: math/LaTeX notation (\geq, frac pieces, '%', 'mod'), 'range' in statistics parentheses, 'Apache' in license headers, 'Id.' in legal citations, CSS/HTML attribute names, and articles in fixed phrases ('named to the', 'off the bench', 'out of'). These do not share an obvious single function.

Mixed. The strongest group is license-header nouns ('LICENSE file', 'license.txt file', 'a copy of', 'FITNESS', 'for licensing details'), and a second recurring pattern is anonymous sources ('did not want/wish to be named'). The rest are miscellaneous content tokens (medical terms, 'dividend', 'Lake', 'née', 'Gen').

Fires on assorted tokens in scientific or technical text, often the second half of a fixed multiword term ('cosmic microwave background', 'upper bound', 'full width', 'A/D converter', '+/-' in mean±SD, 'Collect the terms'). It also fires on random code and identifier fragments (hpet.h, PdfPTable, groups.google), so overall it reads as a mixture.

Fires mostly on the first piece of a capitalized or uncommon word split into several subword tokens, often in non-English or proper-name contexts ('P'ietro, 'B'uhari, 'S'ANTA, 'R'iga, 'r'ife, 'ob'eylines, audi'ob'ooks). It also fires on punctuation in French text. The trigger is mainly the word being an incomplete fragment, with somewhat of a bias toward foreign or multilingual text.

Two strands. The strongest fires on tokens inside Cyrillic (Russian) or CJK text, often a word-initial fragment or preposition. The other fires on English prepositions or particles that link a verb or noun to its argument ('with', 'to', 'by', 'be', 'if', 'off'), e.g. 'pass in a Vector3f with', 'Convert ... to', 'equal to'.

Fires on metadata field keys and markup labels in structured headers: YAML/front-matter keys at line start ('author:', 'title:', 'address:', 'page_title', 'Date:'), '@license', LaTeX '{figure}', and shortcode attributes ('title="..."', 'server='). It responds to the key name or delimiter of a document-metadata record, not to its value.

Strongest and most consistent on 'express' in the Apache license phrase 'either express or implied'. Beyond that it fires on a scatter of unrelated tokens: LaTeX backslashes, template code, size charts ('US'), 'wife', 'received', 'kidney', 'mg', 'around', 'live'. Apart from the license phrase there is no clear pattern.
